paragraphs: Yosef of Maon expounded in their synagogue at Maon—a place-name at Tiberias, hence Maonaya, Mattenot Kehunah—‘Hear this, priests,’ and so forth, concerning the Nasi. Rabbi heard and became angry, because Rabbi was Nasi. Towards evening Resh Lakish went up to greet Rabbi and appeased him concerning Yose of Maon, and so forth: ‘Yose of Maon spoke words of Torah, and you were angry with him.’ He replied: ‘Does he know words of Torah?’ He replied: ‘Yes,’ and so forth. He went up to him. Rabbi asked him: ‘What does “Everyone who uses a proverb about you shall use this proverb, saying, Like mother, like daughter” mean?’ and so forth. He replied, and so forth. Resh Lakish said: ‘I have not yet finished appeasing him for one matter, and now you have added another!’ Jerusalem Talmud, end of Sanhedrin, chapter 2, and Bereshit Rabbah, Vayishlach, beginning of section 80.
